Which expression is missing in the following equation?

$$
(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{1})=[]+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{1})
$$

To find $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{1}),$ we need to find the number that is located in row $3$ and position $1$ of Pascal's triangle. 

**Important**: When counting the rows and positions in Pascal's triangle, we always start counting from zero! Remember:

- The top row of Pascal's triangle is row $0.$

- The first position of each row (the one of the left) is position number $0.$

The location of $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{1})$ in Pascal's triangle is highlighted below.

$$
\begin{aligned} &  &  &  &  &  &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{0}{0}) \\  &  &  &  &  &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{1}{0}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{1}{1}) \\  &  &  &  &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{0}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{1}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{2}) \\  &  &  &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{0}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{1}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{2}) &  & (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{3}) \\  &  &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮ &  & ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Now, $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{1})$ is the sum of the two closest numbers located in the previous row. So,

$$
(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{1})=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{0})+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{1})
$$

Therefore, the missing expression is $(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{2}{0}).$
